subject: Tool calling integration patterns - postcall recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia@finapps.co>; Michael Lopez <michael.lopez@finapps.co>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: tool calling integration patterns & next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Key takeaways:
- Goal: Add structured tool-calling to FinApps’ insights assistant to allow live account lookups, transactions, and PDF export.
- Integration scope: SDK setup + auth (OAuth2 service account or key rotation via KMS), routing to mix of internal microservices and 3rd-party payment API, and embeddings-based reranker for candidate actions.
- Constraints: 200ms median latency target for interactive UI calls; sensitive PII must remain in your VPC (Private mode considered).

Proposed architecture options we discussed:
1) Direct tool calling from runtime (recommended for lowest latency) — Redwood runtime routes to internal tools via secure connectors; use structured JSON schema for tool outputs.
2) Proxy service approach — your gateway receives tool calls and forwards to internal services (easier for existing auth but adds ~80-120ms).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Connor: share sample SDK auth patterns and connector example (by Mon, 8/17) — attaching a small sample.
- Marissa: send tool definition templates + recommended output schema and error-handling patterns (by Mon, 8/17).
- Julia/Michael: confirm which internal services will be callable and whether you prefer service-account OAuth or inbound webhook auth (reply by Tue, 8/18).

Attachments: redwood-tool-calling-patterns.pdf (patterns + error handling checklist), sdk-auth-sample.zip (small connector sample), finapps-map-requirements.xlsx (your notes).

Notes on tool/function calling patterns we recommend (high level):
- Tool definitions: explicit name, input schema, output schema, permissions scope, timeout, retry policy.
- Tool choice: stateless microservices for read-only lookups; stateful transactions through your transactional API with idempotency keys.
- Parallel tools: run independent enrichment tools (embeddings/reranker + credit-check) in parallel and merge via deterministic merge function.
- Error handling: classify transient vs permanent; transient -> retry/backoff; permanent -> user-friendly error + telemetry event; always include fallback LLM-only path.

Happy to jump on a short follow-up to walk through the sample connector and tool definition templates.

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Auth: we prefer service-account OAuth with short-lived tokens minted by our KMS. That keeps keys off-host.
2) Callable services: auth-service, account-lookup, ledger-query, generate-pdf. We’ll provide API specs for each — attaching the current mapping (see finapps-map-requirements.xlsx).
3) Latency: account-lookup needs to be <150ms; ledger-query can be async if needed.

Next steps on our side:
- Michael will pull API owners and confirm endpoints + any existing rate limits (by Wed, 8/19).
- We’d like Connor to share the connector sample you mentioned so our infra team can review auth flows.

Also: could you include a small example of structured output for the generate-pdf tool (schema + example)? That will help our frontend devs.

Appreciate the follow-up.

Thanks Julia — logging responses. Attaching the SDK sample + short patterns doc. Below are the concrete artifacts we’re sending in this email thread so your infra/front-end teams have everything to start a review:

Attachments in this message:
- redwood-tool-calling-patterns.pdf — includes JSON tool-definition templates, structured output examples (including generate-pdf schema), parallel enrichment patterns, and recommended retry policies.
- sdk-auth-sample.zip — example connector showing OAuth2 service-account flow, token refresh, and signed JWT exchange.

Mini structured-output example (generate-pdf):
{
  "tool_name": "generate_pdf",
  "input": {"account_id": "string", "period_start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "period_end": "YYYY-MM-DD"},
  "output": {"pdf_url": "string", "page_count": "int", "checksum": "sha256"},
  "errors": [{"code": "PDF_GENERATION_FAILED", "message": "string", "retryable": "false"}]
}

Error handling patterns (summary):
- Transient (5xx, timeouts): exponential backoff with jitter; mark as retryable and emit telemetry.
- Permanent (4xx validation, permission denied): surface clean error to user and stop retries.
- Partial success: always return canonical output shape with an errors array for downstream merging.

Parallel enrichment example: run embeddings-based reranker and credit-check concurrently; combine results by priority + confidence score; if reranker fails after retries, fall back to model-only ranking and flag for async reconciliation.

Connor will follow up with the connector README and quick walkthrough video link by end of day. If we can get your API specs, we’ll draft the initial tool-definition YAMLs and share a sample PR.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Marissa
